tasks.short: Maintain contractor and client contact and prepare completion and cost reports.

steps.what: Retrieve work progress, commitments and cost records
Maintain contact with contractors and clients about completion and costs
Write the contact record and agreed completion actions
Assess completion risks and practical opportunities to minimise cost
Formulate reports for contractors and clients from the project evidence

loop.purpose: Draft a completion and cost explanation from checked project evidence.
loop.input: Engineer assessment, dated progress and cost records and contact notes.
loop.output: Draft report with source anchors and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Engineer checks numbers, status and commitments against the pack and intended meaning.
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported statements are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies headings but not variable explanations of issues and follow-up.

steps.what: Check the report's technical claims, costs and completion commitments
Send the final report to the authorised contractor or client

tasks.design: Configure project and cost views in {PROJECT} and {ERP}, with a contact template and bounded report draft in {DOCS}. The engineer keeps contractor contact and cost judgement, records agreements, checks the report and separately sends it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress evidence and contact notes must be assembled and rewritten for each report.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and a fixed source pack can simplify retrieval and report drafting.
tasks.still_hard: A low-cost plan can fail if it ignores technical dependencies or unreliable commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile actual progress, contractor accounts and practical completion risks.

ambition.what: Review completion risks between formal reporting dates using the same records.

tasks.altitude: Use report preparation to support practical completion decisions.

reach.learn: Keep progress dates, cost evidence and commitment ownership explicit.

evidence.claim: Native project views and source-bounded report drafting could reduce repeated preparation; this marine-project saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Contact, its record, cost assessment, report writing and report sending are separately counted.

The engineer selects dated progress, cost and contract records in s1 and produces party, date, issue, agreement, owner and due date in s3. Retained 12 and eight hours include selection and capture. Missing or disputed facts remain explicit and are resolved manually.
The s4 engineer supplies the cost and completion assessment; the model cannot invent commitments or claim cost optimisation.
Use native views and templates first. No automated dashboard refresh, ERP write or email send is proposed; internal author editing has no self-approval gate.
unknowns: Existing report templates and quality of dated project and cost records.
research_questions: Does the bounded draft reduce total report preparation after checking costs and commitments?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the report draft.

incremental.description: Maintain views, source links and report drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: Each exact status statement, proposed commitment and cost position communicated during the contact; new terms are checked before communication.
Exact final report and authorised recipient; edits or recipient changes require a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=85, gross=15; upkeep=3 gives central net=12. Contact and cost judgement retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate marine repairs with regulators and record requirements and outcomes.

steps.what: Retrieve regulatory requirements and repair or alteration evidence
Assess repair options for safety, cost and regulatory consistency
Write the repair coordination submission and supporting questions
Send the final repair coordination submission to the regulatory body
Coordinate repair activities and resolve questions with regulatory bodies
Record regulatory responses and required repair follow-up

tasks.design: Configure a requirement-indexed reference view and submission and response templates in {DOCS}. The engineer assesses safety and cost, writes and sends the submission through {EMAIL}, coordinates with regulators and records the outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated evidence retrieval and coordination-document structure consume time around regulatory discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and reusable fields can preserve repair and requirement context.
tasks.still_hard: Regulatory interpretation and safe repair alternatives require technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the engineering position and recognise when a low-cost option is unacceptable.
tasks.altitude: Make regulatory coordination traceable from repair evidence to follow-up.

reach.learn: Distinguish a regulatory response from an engineer's assumption.

evidence.claim: Relatics provides requirements and verification management, supporting traceability as a current capability rather than automated marine regulatory judgement.
Native reference views and coordination templates could reduce clerical work; the labour saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This coordination scenario includes a written submission and subsequent response record; neither is hidden inside the regulatory discussion.

The engineer produces repair identifier, requirement references, proposed position and questions in s3, then response source, date and follow-up in s6. Their retained 15 and four hours include capture and checking. Missing or ambiguous responses require manual clarification.
Try native requirement links and templates first. No machine infers regulatory acceptance, alters equipment or sends a submission.
Internal author writing has no self-approval gate; final-version checks belong to the actual external send and discussion.
unknowns: Actual regulator communication channel and existing submission forms.
research_questions: Does the template reduce preparation without omitting requirement references or unresolved conditions?

already_counted.description: Write and check the coordination submission.

incremental.description: Maintain requirement links and coordination templates.

approvals.approved_version: Exact submission, technical attachments and regulatory recipient; changes require a fresh send-time check.
Each exact technical position or commitment communicated to the regulator; new terms are checked before expression.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=91, gross=9; upkeep=2 gives central net=7. Technical assessment and coordination retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare evidence-based technical reports for engineering, management or sales colleagues.

steps.what: Select checked engineering evidence and define report data fields
Assemble the specified technical report tables and figures
Define the reports' technical conclusions and audience-specific explanation
Draft the technical explanation for the intended internal audience

loop.purpose: Draft an audience-specific technical explanation from selected evidence.
loop.input: Engineer conclusions, outline and identified result passages and tables.
loop.output: Draft explanation with source anchors and stated limitations.
loop.check: Engineer checks each claim, figure reference and number against the evidence and intended conclusion.
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported passages are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed tables cannot explain varied engineering implications for different colleagues.

steps.what: Check and revise the complete technical report
Send the final technical report to the intended colleagues

tasks.design: Use a native report template in {DOCS}, a deterministic table builder from {SPREADSHEET} and a bounded explanatory draft. The engineer owns conclusions, checks the complete report and separately sends its final version through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tables and explanatory prose are repeatedly assembled from checked engineering results.
tasks.enabler_now: Identified source fields support repeatable table preparation and source-bounded drafting.
tasks.still_hard: The same technically correct result can mislead different internal audiences.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the conclusion and explain its limits for the report's intended use.

ambition.what: Prepare another checked internal explanation for a different audience.

tasks.altitude: Spend report preparation effort on implications and evidence checks.

reach.learn: Preserve engineering limitations when communicating applications.

evidence.claim: Native table building and source-bounded explanatory drafting could reduce technical report preparation; the labour saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: These internal technical reports are distinct from contractor or client completion reports in task 21907; actual reused material must be counted once.

The engineer produces source result identifiers, versions, selected fields, units and figure definitions in s1, with all 20 hours of capture and selection counted. Missing or mismatched fields stop the builder for manual correction in s5.
The s3 engineer supplies conclusions and outline. Unsupported claims in the loop return to manual writing in s4; no model chooses engineering conclusions.
Use native templates and table links first. Author edits have no self-approval gate; the real internal send has an exact-version check.
unknowns: Current table automation and intended report mix.
research_questions: Does the combined workflow reduce total preparation after checking source numbers and audience-specific meaning?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the explanatory draft.

incremental.description: Maintain table definitions, templates and source-bound draft checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final internal report and intended colleague list; edits or recipient changes require another send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=67.5, gross=32.5; upkeep=6 gives central net=26.5. Range allows source preparation and extensive technical checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design vessel interior layouts and prepare checked compartment geometry.

steps.what: Establish craft interior requirements, dimensions and access constraints
Design cargo spaces, passenger compartments, ladder wells and elevator arrangements
Enter chosen compartment dimensions and standard component placements
Generate repeated interior component geometry and drawing views
Check and revise interior layout for fit, access and intended function
Save the final interior layout and its model reference version

tasks.design: Use native component libraries and drawing templates in marine CAD software represented by {OTHER}, with requirements in {DOCS}. The architect chooses the arrangement and supplies geometry parameters, then checks generated detail and retains the final save without claiming a saving for it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated compartment geometry and drawing views may be drafted manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parametric components and drawing templates can generate repeat detail from chosen dimensions.
tasks.still_hard: Interior choices affect access, usability, vessel systems and safety.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve spatial trade-offs and recognise when standard geometry is unsuitable.
tasks.altitude: Spend drafting effort on layout choices and integration rather than repeated detail.

reach.learn: Keep geometry tied to checked arrangement and model versions.

evidence.claim: Native CAD component libraries and drawing templates can generate repeat detail; this marine interior-design saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario contains repeated components or views currently drawn manually. Layout choice and checking remain fully human.

The architect produces component type, dimensions, units, placement, orientation and model version in s3, with all ten hours of capture and checking counted. Missing or incompatible parameters stop generation and return to manual editing in s5.
OTHER means existing marine CAD software. Use native libraries and templates before bespoke generation or a model.
The final save retains all its time and has no self-approval gate. No production release, external send or automatic regulatory certification is proposed.
unknowns: Current use of native component libraries and drawing templates.
research_questions: Does native geometry generation reduce total drafting time after fit and access checks on representative interiors?

already_counted.description: Check and revise generated interior detail.

incremental.description: Maintain component libraries and test templates after model changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repeated-detail scenario: B=100, R=80, gross=20; upkeep=5 gives central net=15. Existing native template use reduces the opportunity.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep engineering decisions and external coordination accountable while reducing repeated reports and drawing detail.
reach: Link vessel requirements, contractor commitments, regulatory evidence and technical documents.
role.ambitious_version: A marine engineer or naval architect who can trace layout and project decisions to checked evidence and clear commitments.
